name: Clarios
old_description: Manufactures automotive batteries and energy storage systems (spun off from Johnson Controls).
about:
Clarios was founded in 2019 as a spin-off from Johnson Controls, establishing its headquarters in Glendale, Wisconsin. The company emerged as an independent entity focused on advanced battery manufacturing for the evolving transportation sector.

Today Clarios produces more than 150 million low-voltage batteries each year, employing roughly 7,000 people across a global footprint. Its product portfolio spans absorbent glass mat (AGM), lithium-ion, and supercapacitor technologies, as well as multi-battery architectures that integrate software, electronics, and AI-driven connected services. The company also develops recycled plastics for automotive applications and collaborates on sodium-ion battery industrialization.

The company serves four primary segments: automotive, commercial, powersports, and leisure. Its batteries power one in three vehicles worldwide, reaching customers in over 100 countries through brands such as LTH, MAC, Heliar, Delkor, VARTA, and OPTIMA. Customers include original equipment manufacturers and the aftermarket across passenger, heavy-duty, and recreational vehicles.

Clarios states its mission is to create the world’s best batteries for the future of transportation. It differentiates itself through a chemistry-agnostic approach to low-voltage architectures, integrated electronics and software, and connected services that deliver actionable battery intelligence. Recent initiatives include expanding recycled plastics content and advancing sodium-ion technology with partners Altris and InoBat.
